limitations: Framing is a real utility component, not a production stdio/process adapter, asynchronous bidirectional/pending-call runtime, websocket transport, authentication or negotiated deadline/cancellation. All these remain required product work.

Bodies are opaque; complete framing does not validate JSON. Borrowed and reader-buffered views have distinct documented lifetimes. No retained payload object, callback, lock, timer, Engine or Future is created.

Logical storage includes state and both reusable capacities plus conservative old+new replacement reservations; caller/native buffers, allocator metadata/pools/RSS and later JSON/result copies are outside this bound. Fragmented bodies copy once per input chunk plus actual realloc movement. No universal zero-copy/overhead claim.

Real native stdin/stdout fixtures compose production framing and existing synchronous dispatch with independent Python bytes/JSON/decimal checks. Finite process fixtures do not establish production pipe cancellation/close/backpressure, full bidirectional runtime or physical process-adapter ownership.

One warmup/seven rotated serial unpinned CPU-loop observations with original3% MAD/6% central-range gates; separate heap runs. Raw known-layout control omits header parsing/validation and has no same-function parity/regression gate. Batch-average ns/frame and throughput are not individual P99 or end-to-end transport performance.

No pinned upstream comparison, mixed/fixed-arrival/contention/CPU/RSS/native Linux deployment or>=72h production/performance acceptance. WSL is explicitly not native Linux qualification. All four libraries remain incomplete/developing.
